_comment: Where the raw data comes from. One entry per file the pipeline needs.
STHELAR is on EBI BioStudies, an open FTP, so its URLs are here and the download
stage just works. The 10x Genomics datasets are different: their files are served
behind a form that asks for an email and acceptance of terms, so there is no stable
URL to hard-code and a scripted download would break or, worse, fetch an HTML error
page and save it under a .btf name. For those, `url` is null: the download stage
prints the dataset page and the exact files it needs, and you either fill the URLs in
here once you have them or drop the files in place yourself.
`bytes` is checked after a download when present, because resume turns a truncated
source into a silently short file. The STHELAR sizes were measured from the archive

per_slide.what: SpatialData archive: H&E pyramid, nucleus boundaries, cell expression

visiumhd.note: Three patients, P1 P2 P5. Every URL below was verified with a HEAD request (200, and the Content-Length recorded in `bytes`); P1's tissue image also matched a local copy byte for byte. The dataset page offers the same files behind a form if the CDN layout ever changes. `bytes` is keyed by patient (P1/P2/P5) while {sample} is the full folder name, so sources.visiumhd() takes both.

per_sample.what: square_002um / 008um / 016um; the pipeline reads the 2 um bins

spaceranger spatial outputs (CytAssist image, fiducials). Optional: each bin size carries its own copy, which is what the pipeline falls back to -- P5's local copy has no top-level spatial/ and its run succeeded anyway.
feature slice; not read by this pipeline, listed because the page offers it

xenium.note: The two slides are different Xenium releases and sit under different CDN directories, hence the per-slide `base`. The breast cell-type spreadsheet lives on a different host again and carries its own absolute URL. All verified by HEAD request; the breast H&E and the spreadsheet both matched a local copy byte for byte.

per_slide.what: Xenium output bundle: cells.parquet, nucleus_boundaries.parquet, cell_feature_matrix, experiment.xenium. NOTE the per-slide `strip`: the lung zip has its files at the top level, the breast zip wraps them in outs/ -- see per_slide_extra.breast.

affine aligning the H&E to the Xenium frame. Lung only: breast's published affine is a DIFFERENT alignment, so that slide uses the committed copy in annotations/xenium/ and this entry is skipped for it. See config.XeniumSlide.he_alignment.

breast.what: the published cell-type calls for the breast slide. Served from 10x's media CDN rather than the sample's directory, which is why it is not under `base`; verified 200 / 9,409,803 bytes, sha256 equal to the delivered copy
(overrides per_slide.outputs: this archive wraps everything in outs/)
